# `bin/ledger-claims`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/ledger-claims`](../../../bin/ledger-claims)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/ledger-claims RUN ID [ID ...]

RULES.md step 5. Appends the named claims of RUN to CLAIMS.md at the tag they EARNED
(SCHEMAS.md rules), assigning global ids C-NNN. All-or-nothing: if any named claim is
FALSIFIED, BLOCKED, PENDING, already ledgered, its artifact hash differs from check.json, it supersedes an id
not in CLAIMS.md, or it names a `ledger` premise not in CLAIMS.md, nothing is appended and the reasons are printed.
Per claim it prints, never refusing on them: its model-family line (LESSONS.md "A cross-family certify read"), the notes
on its id and on what it supersedes, the live entries depending on a superseded one (bin/claim-deps), and a MODEL: line
for the run and each referee run not answered by the one model its approval named (LESSONS.md "The model a worker ran
on is recorded").
An entry with `published`, `source` or `ledger` premises carries `(conditional: …)` in its header (SCHEMAS.md §5).

LESSONS.md "Every launch and every ledger append consumes a byte-bound": refuses (exit 3) unless the user ran `bin/approve --ledger RUN ID…` for exactly
these ids within 30 minutes and nothing it bound has changed since: claims.json, check.json,
verdict.md, every live referee.json of these ids, CLAIMS.md. The approval is consumed by the append.
--operator-approved is still accepted and means nothing: the approval record is the approval.
```

- → **A cross-family certify read**
